title: Motilal Oswal AMC Crosses ₹2 Lakh Crore in Assets as Foreign Investors Return to India
excerpt: The asset manager hit the milestone in August, powered by 23 new fund launches in FY2026 and record SIP inflows of ₹16,479 crore — while its group CEO says foreign capital is flowing back.
body:
• Motilal Oswal AMC's total assets under management crossed ₹2 lakh crore ($24 billion) on August 7, 2026, spanning mutual funds, AIF, and PMS.
  • The firm launched 18 passive and 5 active mutual funds in FY2026, adding 56 lakh SIPs with a record inflow of ₹16,479 crore.
  • Group MD Motilal Oswal says foreign investors are returning to Indian equities after two consecutive years of net selling, with July 2026 seeing net inflows again.
  • CEO Prateek Agrawal identifies Make in India as the biggest beneficiary of India's trade deals with the US and EU, arguing that reduced uncertainty is a catalyst for both domestic and foreign capital.

Motilal Oswal Asset Management Company has crossed ₹2 lakh crore in total assets under management, a milestone announced on August 10 that cements the firm's position as one of India's fastest-growing equity-focused asset managers. The figure, recorded as of August 7, spans the company's mutual fund, alternative investment fund, and portfolio management businesses.

For investors tracking India's capital markets recovery, the milestone arrives at a turning point. After two years of persistent foreign selling, Motilal Oswal's group managing director told ANI in August that overseas capital is beginning to flow back.

The Scale of the Achievement

The ₹2 lakh crore mark represents a significant acceleration. As recently as the second quarter of FY2026, the asset management arm had reported ₹1.77 lakh crore in AUM — already a 46% year-on-year increase. The final push to ₹2 lakh crore was powered by strong mutual fund inflows, record SIP additions, and rising participation from both retail and institutional investors.

During FY2026, the company added approximately 56 lakh new SIPs, recording an all-time high SIP inflow of ₹16,479 crore. It also expanded its product line substantially, launching 18 passive mutual funds and 5 active mutual funds across Indian equities, international equities, factor-based strategies, sectoral themes, commodities, multi-asset solutions, and debt.

"Crossing the ₹2 lakh crore AUM milestone is a significant moment in our journey. We have remained committed to building high-growth, earnings-focused portfolios, following our QGLP investment philosophy."

— Prateek Agrawal, MD and CEO, Motilal Oswal AMC

Foreign Investors Are Coming Back

The broader context for the milestone is the shifting tide in foreign portfolio investment. Motilal Oswal, the group's founder and managing director, said at the company's MOBIC conference in Mumbai that July 2026 marked a return to net inflows from foreign investors after two consecutive years of selling.

"When we interact with global investors, the feedback today is that flows are now stabilizing. In fact, looking at the month of July, we have started seeing net inflows again. A lot of investors are coming back and engaging in value buying," Oswal said.

He attributed the shift to greater rupee stability, easing geopolitical tensions, and lower crude oil prices — factors that had previously driven foreign investors toward other emerging markets. Indian mid-cap companies posted profit growth of 27% in 2026, and Oswal expects earnings growth of 15-17% across the broader market this year.

Trade Deals Change the Equation

Prateek Agrawal, the AMC's CEO, has been more specific about the catalysts. In an ETMarkets interview, he identified India's back-to-back trade agreements with the United States and the European Union as potential turning points for the country's manufacturing and investment outlook.

"India already has competitive strengths in manufacturing. Make in India has been a policy focus for a long time, and now, with deals in place with the world's two largest economic blocs, it's a dream come true for the Make in India initiative," Agrawal said.

He noted that India had been the worst-performing emerging market over the previous 12-13 months, with markets like Korea delivering returns of around 80% while India managed single-digit gains. The trade deals, he argued, remove the overhang of uncertainty that had kept foreign allocators on the sidelines.

The first-order beneficiaries of the agreements are limited — textiles, shrimp exporters, and jewellery — but Agrawal emphasized the sentiment effect. Electronics and pharmaceuticals were largely exempt from tariff concerns even before the deals, and the global duty structures for steel, aluminium, and copper remain unchanged. The real shift is in perception: India is no longer seen as being on the wrong side of trade policy.

Where the Money Is Going

Motilal Oswal AMC's investment philosophy, which it calls QGLP — Quality, Growth, Longevity, and Price — remains anchored in high-conviction, concentrated portfolios. Most of its schemes hold between 20 and 35 stocks. Its newer Financial Services Fund, launched in early 2026, tilts toward capital market plays including asset managers, brokers, and exchanges, rather than traditional large banks that Agrawal says are now delivering near-index earnings growth.

The group's private wealth management segment has also expanded, with AUM rising 19% year-on-year to ₹1.87 lakh crore. However, the overall profitability picture is mixed: MOFSL's Q2 FY2026 net profit fell 68% year-on-year to ₹362 crore, hurt by market volatility and lower brokerage income.

Risks on the Horizon

Both Oswal and Agrawal flagged the same concern: dilution. The pace of IPOs and qualified institutional placements continues to accelerate, and supply of new equity could absorb the domestic inflows that have been supporting valuations. "My only worry today is whether there will be too much dilution from IPOs and QIPs because supply is continuing to come," Oswal told ANI. The counterbalance, he added, is the strength of SIP flows and rising household savings finding their way into equities.
